title: Codec Safety Policy Descriptor
description: A sanitized, publishable descriptor for a safety policy enforced by a Codec server. Carries the shape of enforcement (categories, actions, classifier family, summary statistics) but never the contents (individual banned token IDs, classifier thresholds, regex contents). Content-addressed and immutable: a new policy version publishes a new descriptor at a new URL with a new sha256 hash. Symmetric to spec/tokenizer-map.schema.json (text negotiation) and spec/latent-space-map.schema.json (latent negotiation).

id.description: Stable, globally unique policy identifier. Convention: lowercase 'org/policy-name' matching the operator publishing it, e.g. 'acme/strict-v3', 'codec/default-moderate'. Same ID + same hash means byte-identical descriptor. Used as `READY.safety_policy_id` on the wire.

version.description: Schema version. '1' for the current schema (v0.3 launch). Implementations SHOULD reject descriptors whose version they don't recognize rather than silently degrading.

tokenizers.description: Tokenizer IDs (matching `tokenizer-map.schema.json` `id` field) this policy is bound to. A safety policy is tokenizer-specific because banned-id lists, multi-token pattern enumerations, and classifier embeddings are all tokenizer-dependent. A policy that needs to work across tokenizers SHOULD publish one descriptor per tokenizer with a shared id family (e.g. 'acme/strict-v3-llama3', 'acme/strict-v3-qwen2'). Servers MUST reject HELLO if the negotiated `tokenizer_id` is not in this list.

categories.description: Closed list of safety categories this policy enforces. The category names listed here are the names that may appear in classifier output and (in a future additive frame type) in mid-stream policy-violation signaling. Categories are operator-defined but SHOULD draw from a shared registry where possible (see `category_registry` field) to ease cross-policy comparison.

name.description: Category name, lowercase ASCII matching `[a-z0-9_-]+`. Examples: `secrets`, `pii`, `hate`, `jailbreak`, `violence`, `self_harm`.

action.description: Action the server takes when this category fires. `stop` terminates the stream with `finish_reason: "policy_violation"`. `redact` replaces the offending span with placeholder token IDs and continues. `regenerate` rewinds and resamples with the offending IDs masked. `flag` annotates the frame for downstream consumers to act on (server still emits the tokens).

description.description: Human-readable explanation of what the category covers. Useful for client-side audit UI. Plain text, no markdown.

category_registry.description: Optional reference to an external category-name registry the `categories[].name` values are drawn from (e.g. 'mlcommons/ailuminate-v0.5'). Informational only; clients MAY compare categories across policies via this field.

classifier.description: Classifier family that backs this policy's semantic enforcement layer (Layer 3). The descriptor exposes the family: never weights, thresholds, or training data. `family` is enough for an auditor to know what kind of judgments are being made; thresholds and per-category sensitivities are operator-internal.

family.description: Classifier model family. Free-form lowercase ASCII identifier; examples: `llama-guard-3-1b`, `shield-gemma-2b`, `prompt-guard-86m`, `embedding-space-v1`, `none` (rules-only enforcement). New families do not require a schema bump: this is descriptive metadata.

host.description: Where the classifier runs. `server` (typical) means the operator's classifier runs in their deployment. `client` means the policy expects the consumer to run a matching classifier locally (used in mesh/peer-to-peer setups). `both` means the same classifier id is enforced symmetrically by both sides.

requires_engine_features.description: Engine integration features this classifier depends on, declared so auditors know whether the policy is portable across engine forks. Allowed entries: `logits_processor` (banned-id masking), `hidden_states` (embedding-space classifier hook), `sampling_chain` (grammar/FSM mask).

rules_summary.description: Summary statistics describing the size of the enforcement surface, without revealing its contents. Lets an auditor compare policies on coverage breadth (a policy with 20k banned IDs and 50 regex rules is qualitatively different from one with 0 banned IDs and 0 regex rules) without giving an attacker an enumeration map.

banned_token_id_count.description: Number of token IDs in the operator's banned-id list. The IDs themselves are NEVER published.

regex_pattern_count.description: Number of regex patterns enforced (by Layer 1 client prefilter or Layer 2 server post-detok scans). Patterns themselves are NEVER published: they would form an evasion guide.

grammar_constraint_count.description: Number of grammar / FSM constraints enforced via the engine sampler chain.

multi_token_pattern_count.description: Number of multi-token banned patterns (e.g. compiled into an Aho-Corasick automaton over enumerated tokenizations). Pattern strings and their tokenizations are NEVER published.

client_hooks.description: Optional hints to clients about their participation in enforcement. Useful for `@codecai/web-safety` consumers and similar packages: tells them which prefilter checks the operator expects to be run client-side (so a doomed prompt never reaches the wire), and which classifier model id the operator's policy expects (so a peer running its own Layer 3 in a mesh can pick the matching model).

prefilter_categories.description: Category names (matching `categories[].name`) the operator expects clients to enforce client-side before sending. A client without prefilter capability MAY still connect, but the server's enforcement may be the only line of defense for these categories.

client_classifier_family.description: Suggested classifier family for client-side semantic checks. Often a smaller model than `classifier.family` (e.g. server runs `llama-guard-3-1b`, client runs `prompt-guard-86m`). Clients MAY ignore this and pick their own model; this is only a hint.

published_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this descriptor was published. Informational only: content addressing is via sha256 hash.

publisher.description: Optional human-readable publisher metadata. Non-load-bearing; clients SHOULD treat the origin's TLS certificate alone as the trust anchor.

url.description: Publisher home page or audit page.

contact.description: Contact for safety-related inquiries (email, ticket queue URL, etc.).
